teaser.text: S&P Global sells the information, judgments and benchmarks that people use to lend money, invest and price transactions. Its business becomes clearer when you follow both what it sells and the path a customer’s dollar takes.

stock.title: S&P Global stock forecast
stock.meta_description: S&P Global stock forecast: weighted scenarios show where shares could go, what must go right, how much cash the business makes, and what investors pay.
stock.opening: S&P Global's weighted scenario reaches $553.76 in October 2029, after $452.43 in October 2027. It hinges on durable growth, cash generation and disciplined buybacks.
stock.closing: The full S&P Global memo also answers how S&P Global's business works, who its rivals are, how management is allocating capital, and what risks could change the view.

blocks.heading: Where could S&P Global's shares be by 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $452.43 in October 2027, a 12% total return including dividends. It reaches $507.45 in October 2028, a 26% return. By October 2029, it reaches $553.76, a 39% return.

At the final date, the bear and bull outcomes span $320.47 to $838.88. The current price is $408.57. The base case remains the central path, but the range shows how much issuance, AI monetization, leverage, and valuation could matter.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for S&P Global?

paragraphs.text: Healthy issuance, stronger renewals, paid AI adoption, productivity gains and sustained buybacks drive the bull case. Weaker issuance, seat cuts or leverage above target pressure the forecast. The October 27, 2026 results are the first test against the post-Mobility recast history. Through 2027, Market Intelligence renewals and AI-connected products must lift customer spending while leverage moves toward target. The thesis is simple: S&P Global can compound per-share cash growth if its franchises withstand cycles, AI disruption and post-spin leverage.

blocks.heading: How much cash does S&P Global really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow is operating cash after capital spending. In 2025, operating cash fell slightly and free cash flow fell 2.0%, even as net income increased. That does not prove the earnings are fictitious. It means the specialist must inspect the timing of collections and payments.

There are also different claims on the cash. S&P Global’s own free-cash-flow measure deducts $321 million distributed to noncontrolling interests, which belong to outside owners of consolidated businesses. The alternative measure here deducts $236 million of stock compensation, because stock pay gives employees a claim on shareholders’ value. Deducting both would produce a different answer, not a more official one.

blocks.heading: How much does S&P Global pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends add a steadier return component. The current annualized rate is $3.88 per share. The base case assumes 5% annual increases, producing $4.08, $4.28, and $4.49. That is supported by the long record of annual increases and $5,456 million of 2025 free cash flow.

blocks.heading: Does S&P Global's cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The policy later became less extreme but not consistently self-funding. In 2025, shareholder distributions again exceeded free cash flow, acquisitions consumed cash and debt issuance helped support the competing uses. Year-end net debt reached $11,287 million, compared with net cash of $2,394 million in 2021.

blocks.heading: What could change S&P Global's dividend?

paragraphs.text: The bear case freezes the dividend at $3.88 in every period to preserve cash. The bull case assumes 7% increases, producing $4.16, $4.45, and $4.76. That outcome is possible, but it exceeds recent dividend growth while buybacks and debt reduction compete for cash.

blocks.heading: What is S&P Global's dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: The tables show revenue reaching $15,336 million in 2025 while operating margin was 42.2%; the margin story is not smooth. The turn is cash conversion: S&P Global’s own free cash flow was 34.0% of revenue in 2025, down from the prior year. At $408.57, shares offer a 4.5% free-cash-flow yield.

blocks.heading: What has S&P Global guided for 2026?

paragraphs.text: For 2026, management guides to adjusted diluted EPS of $17.50–$17.75 and GAAP EPS of $16.35–$16.60. GAAP is the formal accounting result; adjusted EPS removes specified items, while diluted EPS allows for shares that employee awards could create. Like judging a restaurant, GAAP is the complete bill, while adjusted profit sets aside selected one-time charges. Neither measure is cash available to spend.

The underlying sales target is 6%–8% organic, constant-currency growth. Organic excludes acquisitions and disposals; constant currency excludes exchange-rate movements. Indices is guided to 12%–14% growth and Ratings to 5%–8%, while operating margin should expand by 35–60 basis points. A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point.

blocks.heading: What have S&P Global's last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: Revenue, operating income, net income and diluted EPS all rose from the prior-year quarter, and operating margin widened. The improvement was strongest in Ratings and Indices, where activity benefited from debt issuance and market-linked fees. EPS also benefited from fewer shares, so the operating result matters more than the per-share headline alone.

blocks.heading: What should you watch in S&P Global's next results?

paragraphs.text: S&P Global’s October 27, 2026 announcement will use the new discontinued-operations presentation. Investors should compare each remaining division with its recast history, rather than compare a new total with an old total that still includes Mobility.

The key test is whether revenue growth becomes profit and cash. Ratings and Indices may strengthen the mix, while Market Intelligence and Energy will show whether product improvements and productivity programs are working. An EPS increase funded by stronger operations means something different from one funded by more borrowing.
